_comment: `jobs` is the Nix lane's matrix: one entry per parallel job, and a job
with more than one shard becomes that many jobs. Group suites that
finish in seconds -- their cost is job setup, not testing -- and shard
the ones that do not, so the stage costs what its slowest shard costs.
`native` is the second lane: the platforms Nix cannot reach, which is
where upstream gates. `coverage` is the instrumented lane. `suites` is
how each component's suite is invoked.
`forked` follows upstream, and upstream is not of one mind: ci-settings'
test.py runs every suite one process per test in the container lane,
while angr-management's own ci.yml and coverage.yml run it under
`-n auto` with no --forked at all. This follows each component's own
CI, which is why angr-management is the one suite here that is not
forked -- and forking it is not merely a preference: on macOS a fork
with CoreFoundation already initialised segfaults, which is what it did
here before the setting was corrected.

excluded.tests/exploration_techniques/test_tracer: angr's CGC random-syscall emulation desyncs from the trace that shellphish-qemu 0.12.4's cgc-tracer produces (TracerDesyncError). Deterministic, and unrelated to packaging: the qemu binary runs and unicorn is 2.1.4 as angr pins it. The other 24 tracer tests pass.

tests/engines/test_unicorn.py::TestUnico.reason: unicorn and VEX disagree away from Linux: AngrIncongruencyError, 'Different memory or registers'. It is intermittent and nothing under test moves it: the macOS angr shard 3 of 3 passed this test in run 33175323819 and failed it in the next, 33178855303, over a byte-identical angr tree (1d874555) and the same partition -- both split --splits 3 --group 3 against the committed ci/durations/angr.json, and the two heads differ only in ci.yml, ci/coverage.json and ci/run-native.py. Windows shows the same split: of the five shards that ran it before it was deselected there, three passed and two failed, one with an OSError access violation and one with the same AngrIncongruencyError. The reruns do not absorb this shape: --only-rerun matches the exception text against 'crashed' and 'access violation', an AngrIncongruencyError matches neither, so it fails the shard on one attempt. Upstream runs angr's Windows and macOS suites nightly and gates on neither. Runs and gates on Linux.

tests/exploration_techniques/test_verite.reason: veritesting is unstable on Windows and upstream has the same problem: its nightly failed Test Windows (3) on test_veritesting_b on 2026-08-28, in run 33138392203. Here the module has produced an access violation, a crashed xdist worker, a SimSolverModeError and a bare assertion failure -- different symptoms, one unstable area. The reruns reach only the first two, and by different routes -- a crashed worker is rescheduled on the --reruns budget alone, an access violation matches --only-rerun. The other two match neither regex, so in job 98895004886, with both filters set, the SimSolverModeError and the bare assert each failed on one attempt. Runs and gates on Linux and macOS, where it passes.

tests/test_mcp_server.py::TestMCPLoadBin.reason: passes in every lane that does not instrument. Under --cov the MCP server does not observe the load in time and the test asserts 0 > 0; coverage's tracing changes the timing of a test that talks to a server thread. 626 of angr-management's tests pass unmeasured and 313 of this shard's 314 pass measured.

excluded.tests/test_fuzzer.py::test_multicb_spawn: needs the afl-multi-cgc variant, which the shellphish-afl wheel does not ship -- it carries afl-cgc and afl-unix only, and upstream gets the multi-binary CGC fuzzer from an image that builds AFL from source. Fails with FileNotFoundError on .../bin/afl-multi-cgc/afl/afl-fuzz. The other five phuzzer tests run.
